title: Cold & Wet Job Conditions
short_answer: Mud, paint, and adhesives have temperature floors. Tri-state winters and damp slabs do not care about the schedule — pushing coats into the wrong conditions buys remobilization.
summary: Mud, paint, and adhesives have temperature floors. Tri-state winters and damp slabs do not care about the schedule — pushing coats into the wrong conditions buys remobilization.
plain_words: If it is too cold or too wet for the product, stop and heat, ventilate, or wait. Heater/cans exist on Job Start for a reason. Hero coats in a cold shell look fine at 4pm and fail when the GC walks it under raking light.
when_to_use: Before mud, paint, FRP adhesive, or skim coats in cold or damp conditions
When Job Start heater/cans notes do not match what is on site
After weather delay or standing-by for heat/power
prerequisites: Job Start packet read for heater/cans and power notes
Product labels available (can, bag, or submittal)

tools.name: Heaters / fans per Job Start plan

steps.body: Read the can / bag for min application temperature and humidity. When in doubt, treat 50°F air and surface as a hard floor for compound and most paints unless the product says otherwise.
Surface temperature matters — a cold exterior wall can be below the air temp. Touch the steel; if it feels like a cooler, mud will not dry right.
Heat and ventilate on purpose. Closed-up heat without airflow makes condensation; airflow without heat just moves cold air. Match the Job Start heater/cans note or call the lead.
Protect stocked board from moisture — see Stocking Drywall. Wet board is not "dry enough by morning."
FRP and adhesives are especially unforgiving in cold — do not install to save a day if the adhesive will not cure.
Document delay when conditions stop you — date, hours, reason. Standing-by / weather delay is a record, not a shrug (see Spotting a Change Order).

warnings.title: Do not push coats
warnings.body: Green mud under the next coat, paint over a cold damp wall, and adhesive that never kicks are all the same mistake: the expensive work done twice. QC Walk will catch some of it; the GC's light catches the rest.

quality_checks.prompt: Product min temp/humidity checked on the label
Cold exterior walls / steel checked — not just air temp
Weather or standing-by delay documented same day when work stops

common_mistakes.title: Hero coat in a cold shell
common_mistakes.wrong: Push mud or paint because the schedule is tight
common_mistakes.right: Stop, heat, ventilate, or wait — document the delay
common_mistakes.why: Failures show up under raking light after the crew leaves

common_mistakes.title: Condensation trap
common_mistakes.wrong: Seal the building with heat but no airflow
common_mistakes.right: Match heat and ventilation to the Job Start plan
common_mistakes.why: Wet surfaces fail adhesives and compound cure
